thread.title: Apple Stock Will Rally on a Services Surge, Says Analyst

title: Apple Stock Will Rally on a Services Surge, Says Analyst
text:
Apple Stock Will Rally Because Services Revenue Will Surge, Says Analyst By Dec. 19, 2018 2:43 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Daniel Korpai Text size
Jefferies believes Apple (ticker: AAPL) stock is undervalued after its recent drop over the past two months.
The firm’s analyst Timothy O’Shea reiterated his Buy rating for the smartphone maker’s shares, citing the company’s potential to grow its services businesses.
“While we are reducing iPhone and EPS ests for F’19, Apple’s iPhone business still looks sufficient to build a massive, high margin, high multiple Services business over time,” he wrote on Wednesday.
Apple shares were down slightly to $166.01 on Wednesday.
The analyst is bullish over Apple’s services segment, which includes its App Store, iCloud, Apple Music and Apple Pay businesses. He predicts the company’s App Store revenue will rise to more than $32 billion in five years from just $13 billion this year.
“The opportunity for investors is that these higher-margin, higher-growth software businesses deserve a higher multiple vs the lower margin, lower growth hardware business,” he wrote.
In contrast, O’Shea reduced his iPhone unit sales estimate for fiscal 2019 by 3% to 206 million given recent supplier warnings. As a result, the analyst also lowered his price target to $225 from $265 for Apple’s stock. Still, the reduced price target implies about 36% upside.
He noted how the stock now trades at just 12.5 times forward earnings per share versus the historical 15 times average.
Apple’s shares have declined more than 20% since the end of October as concerns have mounted about weak demand for the iPhone models released this fall.
Earlier this month, Barron’s suggested Apple may want to offer an all-in-one hardware and software subscription offering to generate more stable annual revenue and appease investor concerns over the cyclical nature of iPhone product launches.
